title: PS-6 Predictability of heat stress susceptibility: Correlations between baseline biomarkers and performance indicators in chronically heat-stressed feedlot wethers
content:
Abstract
Heat stress is a barrier to livestock production, disproportionally impacting finishing livestock. Variation in susceptibility causes difficulty in identifying animals at increased risk for morbidity and mortality. Thus, this study aimed to identify baseline biomarkers that predict growth efficiency and physiological stress responses in chronically heat-stressed feedlot wethers. Circulating metabolites, stress biomarkers, and immune factors were analyzed in plasma samples collected from Polypay-crossbred wethers (n=25) before exposure to heat stress conditions (40ºC, THI=86 for 12 h/d; 35ºC, THI=82 for 12 h/d) for 30 d. Bodyweights, ultrasound-estimated back fat (BF) thickness, respiratory rate (RR), and rectal temperature (RT) were evaluated before and after 30 d. Pearson correlation analyses were performed for baseline biomarker associations with growth efficiency metrics: average daily gain (ADG), gain-to-feed ratio (GF), and percent change (Δ%) in ultrasound-estimated loin eye area (LEA) and BF thickness and with physiological heat stress response metrics: Δ%RT, Δ%RR, and Δ% plasma tumor-necrosis factor-alpha (TNFa) from baseline to 30 d. Statistical significance was declared when P≤0.05, and tendencies for significance were declared when P≤0.10. All circulating metabolites were or tended to be correlated with growth efficiency (r = ±0.38–0.57) and with physiological responses (r = ±0.38–0.51). Triglycerides and insulin negatively correlated with GF and tended to negatively correlate with ADG. Insulin-like growth factor-1 negatively correlated with Δ%LEA. Triglycerides, plasma urea nitrogen, and insulin tended to positively correlate with Δ%TNFa, Δ%RR, and Δ%RT, respectively. Cholesterol tended to negatively correlate with Δ%RR. Stress biomarkers were or tended to be correlated with growth efficiency (r = ±0.36–0.56). Partial pressure CO2 positively correlated with ADG and GF, and CO2 and cortisol tended to positively correlate with Δ%LEA. Cortisol tended to negatively correlate with ADG and GF. Epinephrine tended to positively correlate with GF. Immune factors were or tended to be correlated (r = ±0.35–0.41) with physiological responses. Granulocytes and monocytes positively correlated, and granulocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios tended to positively correlate with Δ%RT. Lymphocytes positively correlated with Δ%TNFa. Initial bodyweight tended to negatively correlate with ADG and GF, and RT tended to negatively correlate with Δ%BF thickness. RR negatively correlated with GF and Δ%RR, positively correlated with Δ%BF and Δ%RT, and tended to negatively correlate with ADG. Initial BF thickness negatively correlated with Δ%LEA. These findings indicate that baseline biomarkers exhibit varying strengths of correlation with growth efficiency and physiological responses to chronic heat stress. However, the inconsistencies of individual markers indicate a single marker or type of marker may be insufficient. Thus, a comprehensive baseline panel may be necessary to identify animals at risk for increased morbidity and mortality from chronic heat stress.
